# C# Enum Cheatsheet


## What is an Enum?


An **Enum** (enumeration) is a value type that defines a set of named constants. It makes code more readable and type-safe.

```
Regular Code:          With Enum:
┌──────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐
│ int status=1 │  →   │ Status.Active│
│ int status=2 │  →   │ Status.Paused│
│ int status=3 │  →   │ Status.Closed│
└──────────────┘      └──────────────┘
   Hard to read          Self-documenting
```


```
YourApp.sln
│
├── src/
│   ├── YourApp.Core/              ← Domain/Business Logic
│   │   ├── Entities/
│   │   ├── Enums/                 ← ✓ Enums here!
│   │   ├── Interfaces/
│   │   └── Exceptions/
│   │
│   ├── YourApp.Application/       ← Use Cases/Services
│   ├── YourApp.Infrastructure/    ← External concerns
│   └── YourApp.API/               ← Entry point
│
└── tests/
```


## Basic Declaration


```csharp
// Simple enum (default: starts at 0)
enum DayOfWeek
{
    Monday,    // 0
    Tuesday,   // 1
    Wednesday, // 2
    Thursday,  // 3
    Friday,    // 4
    Saturday,  // 5
    Sunday     // 6
}

// With explicit values
enum HttpStatusCode
{
    OK = 200,
    BadRequest = 400,
    Unauthorized = 401,
    NotFound = 404,
    InternalServerError = 500
}

// Mixed (explicit + auto-increment)
enum Priority
{
    Low = 1,
    Medium,     // 2 (auto)
    High,       // 3 (auto)
    Critical = 10
}
```


## Underlying Types


By default, enums use `int`, but you can specify other integral types:

```csharp
enum Size : byte    // byte, sbyte, short, ushort, int, uint, long, ulong
{
    Small = 1,
    Medium = 2,
    Large = 3
}

// Memory diagram:
// int enum:  4 bytes ████
// byte enum: 1 byte  █
```


## Using Enums


```csharp
// Declaration and assignment
DayOfWeek today = DayOfWeek.Monday;

// Comparison
if (today == DayOfWeek.Monday)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Start of work week!");
}

// Switch statement (recommended)
switch (today)
{
    case DayOfWeek.Saturday:
    case DayOfWeek.Sunday:
        Console.WriteLine("Weekend!");
        break;
    default:
        Console.WriteLine("Weekday");
        break;
}

// Switch expression (C# 8.0+)
string dayType = today switch
{
    DayOfWeek.Saturday or DayOfWeek.Sunday => "Weekend",
    _ => "Weekday"
};
```


## Conversion Operations


```csharp
// Enum to int
int value = (int)DayOfWeek.Monday;  // 0

// Int to enum
DayOfWeek day = (DayOfWeek)3;  // Thursday

// String to enum (parsing)
DayOfWeek parsed = Enum.Parse<DayOfWeek>("Monday");

// Try parse (safer)
if (Enum.TryParse<DayOfWeek>("Friday", out DayOfWeek result))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Parsed: {result}");
}

// Enum to string
string name = DayOfWeek.Monday.ToString();  // "Monday"
```


## Common Enum Methods


```csharp
// Get all values
DayOfWeek[] allDays = Enum.GetValues<DayOfWeek>();

// Get all names
string[] dayNames = Enum.GetNames<DayOfWeek>();

// Check if value is defined
bool isValid = Enum.IsDefined(typeof(DayOfWeek), 3);  // true
bool isInvalid = Enum.IsDefined(typeof(DayOfWeek), 99);  // false

// Get name from value
string name = Enum.GetName(typeof(DayOfWeek), 0);  // "Monday"

// Iterate through enum
foreach (DayOfWeek day in Enum.GetValues<DayOfWeek>())
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{day} = {(int)day}");
}
```


## Flags Enum (Bit Flags)


Use `[Flags]` attribute for enums that can be combined:

```csharp
[Flags]
enum FilePermissions
{
    None = 0,      // 0000
    Read = 1,      // 0001
    Write = 2,     // 0010
    Execute = 4,   // 0100
    Delete = 8     // 1000
}

// Combining flags (bitwise OR)
FilePermissions userPerms = FilePermissions.Read | FilePermissions.Write;

// Checking flags (bitwise AND)
bool canRead = (userPerms & FilePermissions.Read) == FilePermissions.Read;
bool canExecute = userPerms.HasFlag(FilePermissions.Execute);  // false

// Adding flags
userPerms |= FilePermissions.Execute;

// Removing flags
userPerms &= ~FilePermissions.Write;

// Visual representation:
//     Read | Write | Execute
//     ──────────────────────
//      1   |   1   |    0     = Read + Write
```


## Flags Best Practices


```csharp
[Flags]
enum AccessRights
{
    None = 0,
    Read = 1 << 0,    // 1   (bit 0)
    Write = 1 << 1,   // 2   (bit 1)
    Execute = 1 << 2, // 4   (bit 2)
    Delete = 1 << 3,  // 8   (bit 3)
    
    // Combinations
    ReadWrite = Read | Write,
    FullAccess = Read | Write | Execute | Delete
}

// Using bit shift makes it clear and maintainable:
// 1 << 0  →  00001
// 1 << 1  →  00010
// 1 << 2  →  00100
// 1 << 3  →  01000
```


## Extension Methods for Enums


```csharp
public static class EnumExtensions
{
    // Get description from enum
    public static string GetDescription(this Enum value)
    {
        var field = value.GetType().GetField(value.ToString());
        var attribute = field?.GetCustomAttribute<DescriptionAttribute>();
        return attribute?.Description ?? value.ToString();
    }
}

// Usage with Description attribute
enum OrderStatus
{
    [Description("Order is pending")]
    Pending,
    
    [Description("Order is being processed")]
    Processing,
    
    [Description("Order has been shipped")]
    Shipped
}

string desc = OrderStatus.Pending.GetDescription();
```


## Common Patterns


### 1. State Machine Pattern

```csharp
enum OrderState
{
    Created,
    Paid,
    Shipped,
    Delivered,
    Cancelled
}

class Order
{
    public OrderState State { get; private set; }
    
    public void ProcessPayment()
    {
        if (State == OrderState.Created)
            State = OrderState.Paid;
    }
    
    public void Ship()
    {
        if (State == OrderState.Paid)
            State = OrderState.Shipped;
    }
}

// State flow:
// Created → Paid → Shipped → Delivered
//    ↓
// Cancelled
```


### 2. Configuration/Options Pattern

```csharp
enum LogLevel
{
    Trace = 0,
    Debug = 1,
    Info = 2,
    Warning = 3,
    Error = 4,
    Critical = 5
}

void Log(string message, LogLevel level = LogLevel.Info)
{
    if (level >= LogLevel.Warning)
    {
        // Log to file
    }
}
```


## Common Pitfalls & Solutions


```csharp
// ❌ WRONG: Invalid enum value (no compiler error!)
DayOfWeek invalid = (DayOfWeek)999;

// ✅ CORRECT: Always validate
if (Enum.IsDefined(typeof(DayOfWeek), dayValue))
{
    var day = (DayOfWeek)dayValue;
}

// ❌ WRONG: Comparing strings directly
if (day.ToString() == "monday")  // Case-sensitive!

// ✅ CORRECT: Use proper parsing
if (Enum.TryParse<DayOfWeek>("monday", true, out var parsed))
{
    // ignoreCase = true
}

// ❌ WRONG: Flags without [Flags] attribute
enum BadFlags { A = 1, B = 2, C = 4 }
var combo = BadFlags.A | BadFlags.B;
Console.WriteLine(combo);  // Prints "3" (confusing!)

// ✅ CORRECT: With [Flags] attribute
[Flags]
enum GoodFlags { A = 1, B = 2, C = 4 }
var combo2 = GoodFlags.A | GoodFlags.B;
Console.WriteLine(combo2);  // Prints "A, B" (clear!)
```


## Quick Reference Table


| Operation | Syntax | Example |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Declare | `enum Name { ... }` | `enum Color { Red, Green }` |
| Assign | `EnumType var = EnumType.Value` | `Color c = Color.Red` |
| To int | `(int)enumValue` | `int x = (int)Color.Red` |
| From int | `(EnumType)intValue` | `Color c = (Color)1` |
| Parse | `Enum.Parse<T>("Name")` | `Enum.Parse<Color>("Red")` |
| Try parse | `Enum.TryParse<T>("Name", out var)` | `TryParse<Color>("Red", out c)` |
| Has flag | `value.HasFlag(flag)` | `perms.HasFlag(Read)` |
| Add flag | `value \|= flag` | `perms \|= Write` |
| Remove flag | `value &= ~flag` | `perms &= ~Execute` |


## Best Practices Summary


```
DO:
  ✓ Use enums for fixed sets of related constants
  ✓ Use [Flags] for combinable values
  ✓ Use power of 2 for flags (1, 2, 4, 8...)
  ✓ Include None = 0 for flags enums
  ✓ Validate enum values from external sources
  ✓ Use meaningful names
  
DON'T:
  ✗ Use magic numbers instead of enums
  ✗ Change enum values after deployment
  ✗ Forget [Flags] attribute for bit flags
  ✗ Trust unchecked casts from int
  ✗ Compare enum.ToString() directly
```
